name: THE SCHOOLHOUSE
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE DESKS
LOOK_AT: Fourteen desks, made by hand, well made. Nobody has ever sat in them.
Each desk has an inkwell, filled. The ink has dried in every one, waiting.
The lids are carved: not by children, by the carpenter, with the date. Every desk is dated the same day.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Fourteen desks, and not a whisper among them.
A lid, settling, very quietly, as if it had nearly been opened.

overrides.PUSH: They're in perfect rows. I'm not going to be the one who spoils that.

subjects.name: THE BLACKBOARD
LOOK_AT: Blank. It has been washed. Somebody washed a blackboard that has never been written on.
There's chalk on the ledge, a whole new box, unopened.
The board's been oiled, so the chalk would take. It's ready for the alphabet, and the alphabet hasn't come.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. A blackboard is quiet until somebody makes it squeak.
Nothing. I'm not going to make it squeak. It deserves better for a first word.

overrides.USE: I'd write something, but the first thing on that board ought to be the alphabet, not me.

subjects.name: THE BELL ON THE DESK
LOOK_AT: A brass handbell on the teacher's desk, for calling in a class that hasn't come.
Polished. Somebody comes in to polish a bell that has never been rung for a class.
The handle is turned wood, and fits a hand exactly. A teacher's hand. It's waiting for one.
LISTEN_TO: …It's in tune. Of all the things in this town.
Still in tune. I've come back to check twice.
Nothing. I'm not going to ring it. Not for nobody.

overrides.USE: No. The first time that bell rings, it should mean something.

subjects.name: THE STOVE
LOOK_AT: A school stove, blacked and cold, with the kindling laid ready in it. Ready for winter, and for children.
The coal scuttle's full, and the coal's never been touched. It's the best-stocked stove in town.
A kettle on top, clean, for a teacher's tea. There's a cup beside it, for one.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. A cold stove sounds exactly like an empty room.
Nothing. It's waiting for winter, and for someone to be cold in front of it.
A tick of iron, cooling further. It has never once been warm.

subjects.name: THE WINDOW
LOOK_AT: Clean glass. Through it, the town, which is busy looking for gold and has never once glanced this way.
The glass is new and the putty's still pale. Built well, and built for children who'd want to look out.
A teacher at that desk would see the whole town at once, and know exactly who was late.
LISTEN_TO: The hammering from town, far off. Everybody is building something, and not this.
Somebody hammering, very far off. Consolation builds at all hours, except in here.
Wind across the glass. It's the only lesson the room has ever had.

subjects.name: THE DOOR
LOOK_AT: The schoolhouse door, on new hinges that have never once been opened by a child.
A hook on the inside for each coat. Fourteen hooks. They counted.
There's a little step outside it, low, for short legs.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing, which in a schoolhouse is the saddest sound there is.
The hinges, silent. They've been oiled, for nobody.
Nothing. It's been holding the door for a class for years.
